Adds a new `viola focus <name>` CLI verb: resolve the home, validate the name, read the instance's state under the strict-modes checks, find the session's window and bring it forward on its workspace through the closed Hyprland request set only.
Window identity comes from the window recorded for a session `viola open` started, or for a hand-started `viola run` from the wrapper's process ancestry matched against the compositor's client list.
Every no-window outcome ends in a named refusal, and outside Hyprland the verb refuses as unsupported; refusal words, exits and hints are added beside the existing refusal, exit-code and help tables.
Tests run on the fake compositor's recorded replies and the fake agent; no live start, window, dispatch or key in this phase.

body: The new verb appears in `viola --help` as a served verb with its own row under the existing group labels and usage line.

Every focus refusal (no session, no window found, a recorded window that is gone, unsupported outside Hyprland) prints in the CLI refusal form: an unable line with its kebab-case reason code beside a plain word, then exactly one hint line, on stderr.
Each new refusal code carries its one hint, no hint names a release, and an unlisted code word stays visible; the `unknown` refusal keeps no hint.

Each focus refusal maps to an exit code from the existing CLI exit-code table (usage error exit 2 for a bad name, the instance-unreachable and refusal exits as they stand), or a new code entered beside them.
Under --json a focus failure is one clean failure document with no hint and no SGR, its code and exit matching the human form.
An unstattable or wrongly-moded home, or socket directory, is a strict-modes refusal before any read of state or any Hyprland request, with its instance-unreachable detail word.
The name printed in any focus line or refusal is the parsed, validated argument, never a value read back from the compositor or the snapshot.

Any text from the compositor's replies or the snapshot (window address, workspace name, client title) that reaches output is screened: C0 and C1 control characters printed escaped, compositor replies screened to code words.
Focus output is static and linear: a single result or refusal in one write, no spinner, no progress line, no interactive prompt.
Failure and refusal words are never coloured; no SGR off a colour-capable terminal or under --json, and any SGR only beside its word.
No time bound falls on the human: any wait on the compositor's reply is a bound on the driver only, and no new time bound is added while that question stands open.
Error messages carry a word, detail and hint shape; thiserror messages interpolate nothing and no stack trace or bare status is the error text.
Each fixed focus string (refusal words, hints, help row) comes from the design copy and is pinned by its literal in a test.
Focus moves the operator's window focus only through the compositor; it writes no byte to any wrapped session's terminal and sends it no key.
Clauses the fakes cannot carry (a live window raised on the host) are a live reading that never gates and is planned gated on the operator's grant.

body: The TUI passthrough contracts of `viola run` (entry, human keystrokes, focus, mouse and resize sequences, vt100 feed panic, run diagnostics): focus never enters the wrapped session's terminal stream.
The `viola list` board rows (caption order, colour, stale-row dim, NAME truncation, unwrapped separator, empty board): focus prints no board.
The `viola revive` refusals, --list output and start-against-a-holder refusals: focus starts and revives nothing.
The `viola link` and `viola unlink`, `viola plugin install`, `viola send`, `viola wait` and `viola verify` output rows: other verbs whose output focus does not change.
The hook event and dialog call rows and the dialog hold in config: focus raises no dialog and answers none.
The manual screen-reader and keyboard passes and their Orca setups: supplemental, gating nothing this chunk builds.
The absences of a web or graphical frontend, a touch surface, internationalization and a rendered page: none reached by a CLI verb.
The structured violation JSON schema rows: the CI report shape is unchanged by a new verb.

**2026-11-14-hyprland-seam** (Standard Contracts · Conventions · Infrastructure Patterns · Occupied Resources) — added `decision/hyprctl-direct-spawn` (direct spawn from a caller-resolved path, no shell, no PATH lookup, closed argv, Lua dispatch with only a closed address or i32 inserted), the five closed `contract/hyprland-seam-errors/*` words (unsupported · unreachable · oversize · malformed · refused, fixed messages interpolating nothing), `decision/hyprland-seam-crate` (viola-hyprland sync, tokio-free, depends on viola-core alone), the `malformed` exception on `decision/unparseable-external-values-unknown`, and the names `viola-hyprland` / `viola-hypr-tap`; it also cut «depends on all members» from `decision/root-bin-consumes-normalised-events` because viola-hyprland was a root dev-dependency only «while no verb calls the seam». Matters: `viola focus` is the first product verb to call the seam, so it makes viola-hyprland a real root dependency, must go only through the closed request set, and must map every seam error word to a named refusal, with `unsupported` as the outside-Hyprland case.

**2026-11-23-seam-requests-for-viola-open** (Standard Contracts, two entries) — widened `decision/hyprctl-direct-spawn` from the single `hl.dsp.focus` form to one Lua element, `hl.dsp.focus` or `hl.dsp.window.move`, measured live on Hyprland 0.56.2. It also changed the why: Hyprland runs dispatch arguments as Lua, so only the measured forms are accepted (PROVISIONAL, delegate viola-overseer). Matters: focus's «show the workspace and raise the window» must stay inside these measured forms. A workspace-focus dispatch that is not `hl.dsp.focus` on an i32 would be a new form to measure and record, and the scope's premise that the seam holds a workspace-focus dispatch must be re-measured against this row.

**2026-11-23-viola-open-2** (Standard Contracts · Conventions · Established Decisions · Occupied Resources) — landed the window record that focus's identity arm (a) reads: `contract/instance-snapshot/window` (`{address?, workspace?, placement, origin}`, rebuilt by replay from the last `window` line after the last `launch` line, a later `launch` clearing it), `contract/event-data/window`, `contract/wrapper-event-appends/window` (one line only under `--origin`, log-only, never waking `wait`), `window` among the replay's recovered fields, and `window?`/`origin?` on list items. It also added the `viola open` exit codes 0/1/2, put open's refusals under `contract/cli-exit-codes/1`, added the process-exit details `terminal-not-found` and `not-live` to the diag-line enum, added the hidden `run --origin` / `--place` flags, and extended `decision/no-start-over-live-instance` to open. Matters: these are the precedent for focus's refusal words, exits and detail-enum entries, and they confirm that a hand-started `viola run` records no window, so focus needs the ancestry arm.

**2026-11-08T20-32-52-wrap** (version census 0.2.0) — removed every web and graphical surface: there is no page and no graphical control surface, and the view beyond `viola list` is a keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland, owed by later Epoch 6 entries. Matters: it backs the picked absences (graphical frontend/interface) and `decision/window-features-target-hyprland`. Focus is a compositor action, not a GUI, and must not grow into a console surface.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (OS target · OS-gate census · no-shell-out) — made viola Linux only, with the 0.2.0 window features on Hyprland and Windows and macOS recoverable at `multi-os-final`. Nothing shells out through `sh`/`bash`. The OS-gate census now treats a gate whose predicate names `windows` or `target_os = "macos"` as a fault even when named. Matters: it is the source of `decision/linux-only`, `decision/window-features-target-hyprland`, `decision/no-other-os-test-gates` and `decision/os-gated-tests-name-reason`. Any test gate focus adds needs its `GATES` row in `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` and may name no other OS.

**2026-11-04-linux-and-macos-parity** (the OS-gated tests census) — added `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` with its `GATES` table: every OS-gated test function or gated file needs a row with a non-empty reason, and the census fails on an unnamed gate and on a stale row. Matters: it is the origin of the picked `decision/os-gated-tests-named` guard. Fake-compositor or Hyprland-only tests for focus must land with their rows.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (exit 21 causes · code-word rule · exit-cause table · process-exit enum) — made exit 21's `detail` the closed `UnreachableCause` word, written only by `client::unreachable_document`. Added `liveness::without_endpoint`: an instance directory reads `instance-dead`, anything else `unwrapped-name`. Gave `stale-heartbeat` its own exit-1 code. Required every exit-21 cause and exit-1 code to pass `is_code_word` and be a row of `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` and `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` (`no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, `every_code_is_a_code_word`). Added the `--json` internal-error document at the `cli` catch site and widened the diag-line `process-exit` detail enum. Matters: every new focus refusal word, its hint and its document must join these tables and the schema enum, and focus's «no live wrapper» reading should reuse `without_endpoint`'s split rather than invent one.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (`socket-dir-refused`) — added `socket-dir-refused` as exit 21's sixth cause, a closed word with no path. Its human pair names only the parsed `ViolaName`, is plain ASCII with `hint:` last, and its hint sits in `src/human/hints.rs`. `viola list` moved to one read rule on the home. Matters: this is the pattern for adding a closed refusal word with its hint and sanitised pair (`contract/exit-21-human-hints/placement`). It also shows that a cause set grows by named members, not by reusing an existing word.

**2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded** (Conventions) — rewrote `contract/unreachable-cause/cause-set` as a closed set of seven, adding `CallDeadline` as `call-deadline`, written by the MCP frame tools alone and kept apart from the six exit-21 causes. Added `call-deadline` to the MCP `instance-unreachable` detail list. Matters: focus's refusals must not be folded into `UnreachableCause` by accident. A new cause is a ruled change to a closed set that the picked rows hold.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (strict-modes first · readers on the replay) — made the instance's strict-modes check (`client::refuse_untrusted`, `check_instance`) the first step of every CLI frame verb, ahead of any role file, log or snapshot read. A refusal is exit 21 with `strict-modes-failed`, writes no line and leaves the mode as found. It also moved every snapshot reader onto `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, so a replayed snapshot gives no endpoint and `read_snapshot` has no product caller. Matters: focus reads the instance's snapshot, so it must take the check before any read or log (`decision/instance-check-before-any-read`, `decision/strict-check-before-log-open`). It must read the snapshot through the replay, where a replayed `window` comes from log lines, and it writes one `state-recovered` line.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (the instance check before any log, on both arms) — measured the trap behind the rule: opening a log narrows an existing home to 0700, so a check made after the log opens passes a home at 0770. It moved revive's and hook statusline's checks ahead of their logs, and a refused check writes no line. Matters: this is the reason for the picked `decision/instance-check-before-any-read` and `decision/strict-modes-check-before-log`. Focus's order must put the check first.

**2026-10-26-explicit-session-links** (the link verbs) — built `viola link` / `viola unlink` as CLI-only human controls. They run `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` before any role file or log (exit 21, no line, mode as found), write `cli-<driven>.ndjson` only after the check passes, and use one shared args struct with `[--json]`. Matters: this is the nearest precedent for a new CLI-only human-control verb (`decision/human-controls-cli-only`, `decision/pause-link-unlink-cli-only`). It gives the order and log rules for the scope's conservative «CLI-only, no MCP `focus` tool» arm.

**2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list** (caller-side board) — made `list` a caller-side reader of `<home>/instances/` that contacts no wrapper. Its scan checks the home and each instance before any open and any log, and a failure refuses the whole board with exit 21 and no line. The replay counts as a reader, giving `live` for a replayed snapshot only on a fresh beat. Matters: focus, like list, reads instance state without a live channel. The board's reading of replayed snapshots and liveness is the model for deciding whether a target is live before acting on its window.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** (the snapshot's pid and started_at as identity) — made the snapshot's `pid` plus OS `started_at` the wrapper's identity, compared in whole seconds through `liveness::verify_server`, because a bare pid is reused. Matters: focus's ancestry arm starts from a pid known from the snapshot (wrapper or `child_pid`). The pid must be matched with its start time, per `decision/liveness-heartbeat-and-pid` and `decision/session-liveness-heartbeat-and-start-time`, before the compositor's client list is walked by ancestry.

**2026-11-22-lineage-registry** (Established Decisions · Standard Contracts) — added `decision/lineage-label-only`: lineage is a label no wheel, link, send or answer path reads, held by a source census guard (`lineage_is_read_by_no_wheel_link_send_or_answer_path`). It also added lineage to the snapshot and the replay. Matters: the scope's «by recorded identity or ancestry» means process ancestry. Focus must not resolve a window through the declared parent or role, or it widens the label-only rule.

**2026-11-23-model-and-effort-at-launch** (Standard Contracts) — added the `launch` kind and the snapshot's `launch?` field, recovered by replay from the last `launch` line. `window`'s replay rule is defined relative to it: a later `launch` clears the window. Matters: when focus reads a replayed snapshot's window it depends on this rule. A revived or restarted instance's old window is cleared, so a recorded window can be absent or stale, which is the «recorded window that is gone» fork.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (Cross-cutting Patterns · Conventions) — added `decision/sanitised-error-surfaces`: CLI `--json` documents, MCP error results and channel error data carry codes and fixed messages only, with no path, pid or upstream text. The census `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` requires every error body to name its writer and a witness, `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` is held, and a peer's text reaches a surface only as a closed value. Matters: focus's refusal documents and its hyprctl-derived failures, where reply text is upstream content, must be closed words. Each new body needs its table row, or the census goes red.

body: A new CLI verb `focus` joins the CLI verbs boundary and the command name register. It is added as a subcommand in the existing clap flag and subcommand style, with its argument shape among the viola CLI arguments.
The `<name>` argument is validated through ViolaName as the instance key, so control characters are refused and never stripped. Identity comes from the instance, never from a location.

The viola home is resolved in the viola home resolution order. The strict-modes read rule applies before any read of instance state or logs. A failed check writes no line and refuses with exit 21 strict-modes-failed and its exit-21 human hint.

The verb reads the instance snapshot: the snapshot envelope and its version, the `window` field (address, workspace, placement, origin) the wrapper records only under `--origin`, and the pid fields. Reads are versioned-tolerant, a missing value and a null read the same, and a replayed or unreadable snapshot is handled as the snapshot rules say. The verb writes no file.
First identity source: a recorded window address is re-parsed through the Hyprland seam's Address validator before use, and recorded text is treated as untrusted upstream text.

Second identity source, for a hand-started session with no recorded window: the wrapper's process ancestry is matched against the compositor's client list. This goes through viola-state's ancestry walk if it can be reused (at most 8 parent pids, held in memory), starting from a pid the snapshot holds. Lineage stays a label only.

Every compositor call goes only through viola-hyprland, the one compositor seam, and its closed request set: a workspace-focus dispatch and a focus-window dispatch. hyprctl is spawned directly with a closed argv and nothing shells out. Window features target Hyprland.
The Hyprland seam's errors (unsupported, unreachable, refused, malformed, oversize) each map to a named refusal of the verb. Outside Hyprland the verb refuses as unsupported.

Every no-window outcome gets a named refusal: the recorded window is gone, no client matches, or the name holds no instance. Each one adds an entry to the closed sets beside the existing tables: the CLI exit codes, the process-exit detail enum (next to terminal-not-found), the --json error document and the human refusal line. The usual rules hold: refusal details come from a closed set, only the first refusal is returned, wire enum values are kebab-case, and retired exit codes are never reused.

Output follows the CLI conventions: human text by default and a `--json` document for agents. Refusals go on human stderr through the one human writer, with no print macros. Error surfaces are sanitised, and the role's codes-only process log (the cli-<name> diagnostics role file) holds codes only.
Errors follow the crate rule: thiserror in the crates, with messages that interpolate nothing, and anyhow only at the root bin edge.
Focus stays CLI-only, a human control. No driver-session surface may move the operator's focus unless a ruling widens the boundary.
The verb grows no new time bound and no new full time-bound list cell. That question waits on the operator's open fork.

Tests prove the verb against the fake compositor (viola-hypr-tap's recorded replies for Hyprland 0.56.2) and the fake agent, with no live claude, no live compositor, no real window moved and no read of the operator's real claude home. body: The new command name focus joins the register of CLI verb names as a flat verb beside open, list, send and the rest, and takes its place in the viola --help verb groups.

The session name argument is validated before any read, and a name that is no wrapped session is refused the way the other instance verbs refuse an unwrapped name: unwrapped sessions are never a target.
The instance's state is read under the strict-modes checks; a strict-modes failure refuses with the fixed instance-state unable/hint pair and its exit 21 cause, as the other frame verbs do.

Window identity, recorded arm: the window record a session started with --origin carries (address, workspace, placement, origin) is read back, and its address is re-parsed before use rather than trusted; the origin and placement words it carries are the existing fixed vocabularies.

Window identity, ancestry arm: for a hand-started viola run the wrapper's process ancestry is matched against the compositor's client list, bounded by the existing in-memory ancestry walk's limit of parent pids.
The focus and workspace moves go only through the Hyprland seam's closed request set: no other call to the compositor, no dispatch outside that set, and no key sent.

A named refusal for every no-window outcome, and an unsupported refusal outside Hyprland: each on the fixed refusal line form on stderr with its exit code from the CLI exit-code table and its cause word, the words and exits fitted beside the existing tables.

Each refusal cause carries at most one hint, in human mode only, that never quotes text, never names viola release, and shows no path, pid, window address or other internal; faults and unknown causes carry no hint.
Success is announced only after the compositor confirms the window was brought forward, and the confirmation line carries the session it acted on; nothing optimistic before the reply.

Output discipline: data on stdout, messages on stderr; ASCII-only words, no glyph or emoji prefixes, control characters in any echoed session name escaped, no spinner, no interactive prompt or pager, no stack traces.
Colour follows the CLI colour decision order and is limited to amber and dim, decided by std IsTerminal TTY detection, NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb, with no background colour set.

If the verb takes --json, its result is one stdout document, its failure documents clean with the cause code and no hint line, and the catch site's --json scope and internal-error document apply to it.
CLI-only boundary: the verb is for the human and the LLM driver as CLI callers; no MCP focus tool is added and the hidden mcp verb gains nothing.

body: A new short-lived cli verb, `viola focus`. It is a cli role process that writes its own process log, and only under a name parsed as a ViolaName. It gets one manual dispatch span, a process-start line and a process-exit line carrying an exit code and a detail code.

The instance comes from the name the verb is given, never from the working directory. The home is resolved in the fixed order, and the home-tree and strict-modes checks run before the cli log opens. A strict-modes refusal that comes before the log opens writes no line and leaves with the existing strict-modes-failed exit codes and stderr pair.

Reading the instance's state: the verb reads the snapshot's window record (address, workspace, placement, origin) through replay, never raw. A snapshot rebuilt by replay carries no live endpoint. Entries the reader rejects or skips (symlinks, unknown keys, torn lines) surface as parse-rejected counts, never as content.

The Hyprland seam as a child process: the compositor probe is the hyprctl-probe spawn subject. Its JSON replies (the client list, dispatch replies) are untrusted. A reply or a recorded window address that fails to parse surfaces as unknown, with a parse-rejected line for the hyprctl-json parser and a closed detail word.

New refusal causes: no window found, a recorded window that is gone, and unsupported outside Hyprland. Each needs its own closed exit detail code, distinct per cause, with no path, pid, window address or workspace in it. Each reaches stderr as a fixed unable/hint pair, and reaches the --json error document as a closed code.

The ancestry arm reuses the state crate's in-memory walk of at most 8 parent pids. That walk is instrumented synchronously without Tokio. The pids it walks and the window addresses it matches are never logged as values in detail codes or in home-level lines.

Only typed low-class fields are logged on the focus path: the window address, workspace, client list rows and process ancestry stay out of home-level lines. Anything content-bearing goes only to the instance detail file. Error chains reach stderr as fixed messages, with no serde source in them.

A panic in the cli role while focusing: the panic hook is installed first, the panic is recorded as one line, and the exit is decided at the catch site. The panic outcome for the cli role (human and --json) applies to the new verb.
The cli role's stdout carries only the verb's result, with no telemetry on it. Terminal rendering of any compositor-supplied text escapes control characters.
Each Hyprland dispatch is issued once and never retried: retry policies and retry-once are forbidden. No new time bound is added while the operator's fork on time bounds stands.

The tests read the recorded Hyprland replies through the fake compositor. Those fixtures are not a telemetry source. Every line the new tests make the binary emit is checked against the diagnostic schema, and the zero-panics gate reads those lines. The tests wait on logs by condition, never by sleep.
Linux is the only OS target. On a host that is not running Hyprland, focus must refuse as unsupported and must not start the compositor probe.

The snapshot's window record (address, workspace, placement, origin) is a reference value read only after the strict-modes check and re-parsed before use; a recorded window or its origin authenticates nothing, and the record stays kept to the snapshot and the event log — focus copies it nowhere else.

State readers never write: focus reads the snapshot written only by the instance's wrapper and writes no state file, stamp, trust record or log line under the home of its own beyond what the logging rules admit.

The compositor is reached only through the Hyprland seam's closed request set: the focus-window and workspace-focus dispatches recorded for Hyprland 0.56.2, the hyprctl child spawned directly and bounded by a deadline, its reply text dropped at the parse and only closed values kept.

The ancestry arm: the wrapper's process ancestry walked through the existing in-memory walk (at most 8 parent pids, process identity through sysinfo) and matched against the compositor's client list; a self-reported parent, lineage or launch pair authenticates nothing, and no pid leaves memory.

Compositor client-list text (titles, classes, workspace names) is upstream content, never a command, read through a bounded reader and screened to closed values; a new external reader is bounded or named in the bounded-readers census and capped at the shared frame limit.

Detecting Hyprland (the unsupported arm) reads the compositor's environment; a new environment read or seam needs its log entry, environment variables are only compared and are never configuration, and no flag, env var or config switches the checks off.

The new named refusals (no window found, a recorded window gone, unsupported outside Hyprland) and their exits join the CLI exit-code and exit-cause tables; refusal and error text holds no paths, pids, ids or window addresses, interpolates nothing, carries no upstream text and maps parser errors to fixed messages.

Every new product error writer of the verb is named, under the error-enum convention and its named exceptions; an internal error is held at the unit layer and the verb's catch-site internal error output follows the --json form.

body: A new CLI verb, viola focus, tested as a subprocess of the real viola binary in a fresh per-test home, its outputs pinned by literal asserts.
The verb's name argument is validated as a viola name before any read; an invalid or control-character name is refused, never used as a target, and human output escapes control characters.
The instance's state is read under the strict-modes checks before any read or open: a home or instance another user may read is refused with the strict-modes refusal, as for every other CLI verb.

The snapshot is read only through the read-or-replay path; a replayed snapshot carries no endpoint and no window, and the verb must act on that (the window record is read only from the snapshot the wrapper wrote).
Window identity arm (a): the window record the wrapper keeps under --origin (address, workspace, placement, origin), its address re-parsed through the seam's address validator before any dispatch.

Window identity arm (b): for a hand-started viola run with no window record, the wrapper's process ancestry (a bounded in-memory walk of at most 8 parent pids) matched against the compositor's client list.

Hyprland dispatches only through the hyprland seam's closed request set: a workspace-focus dispatch and a focus-window dispatch, recorded for Hyprland 0.56.2 and replayed by the fake compositor; no other request is sent.

Named refusal for every no-window outcome (no window found, recorded window gone, no ancestry match, instance not wrapped or not live) and an unsupported refusal outside Hyprland, each a distinct exit cause with its own hint, in both human and --json modes, one JSON document per run.
CLI exit codes and exit-cause table gain the focus refusals; the --json failure document and human refusal lines carry them, error bodies sanitized with no path or upstream text.
viola --help grouped verb table gains the focus verb; help carries no bold or underline and no SGR without a terminal.

Tests reach the compositor only through the fake (recorded replies, a real stub process or seam double), never a live Hyprland; the real window placement and focus are proven only live and that clause is planned gated on the operator's live reading.
Test-started viola drops inherited session and VIOLA_* environment variables, and the Hyprland signature environment the verb reads is set per child, never by process-wide env mutation.
Tests never read the host's claude sessions or real home; viola list or focus runs only against the fake agent on a test-scoped PATH, with no real claude in CI.
CLI-only: focus is not added to the MCP tool set (no control tools over MCP); the MCP tools/list stays as it is.
No new time bound: any wait on the compositor reply stays inside the existing bounded readers and wait bounds, no sleeps or retries in tests.
Fixtures for the compositor replies are recorded, scrubbed of real data (no addresses, usernames or home paths of the host) and byte-compared; the fake replays them byte for byte.
Error sanitization and log lines: any process log or diagnostics line the verb writes is structured JSON, codes-only, carrying no session names or secrets.
